title: The atomic embedding proof attributes atomicity to the wrong model.
details: Theorem7.9(1), printed p.85, uses atomicity of N in the one-point extension even though only the source model M is assumed atomic and the target N is arbitrary. The isolating formula must be chosen from the type of the source tuple in M. Partial elementarity transfers its existential assertion to N, where a witness realizes that isolated joint type. This local wrong-model reference is repairable; the theorem and its arbitrary-target conclusion remain valid. The corpus chooses the joint isolator from M explicitly and retains the supplied finite map.
